source_text: Κατηγορεῖ δ᾿ ὁ Κέλσος καὶ τοῦ φάσκοντος λόγου ἄγγελον ἀποκεκυλικέναι τοῦ τάφου, ἔνθα ἦν τὸ Ἰησοῦ σῶμα, „τὸν λίθον“ ὥσπερ μειράκιον, ἐν διατριβῇ λαβὸν τοπικῶς κατηγορῆσαί τινος, καί φησιν ὡς σοφόν τι κατὰ τοῦ λόγου εὑρὼν [καί φησιν] ὅτι ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ παῖς, ὡς ἔοικεν, οὐκ ἐδύνατο ἀνοῖξαι τὸν τάφον, ἀλλ᾿ ἐδεήθη ἄλλου ἀποκινήσοντος τὴν πέτραν. καὶ ἵνα γε μηδὲν περιεργάσωμαι περὶ τῶν κατὰ τὸν τόπον μηδὲ τροπολογίαν ἐπὶ τοῦ παρόντος ἐκτιθέμενος δόξω ἀκαίρως εἰς ταῦτα φιλοσοφεῖν, περὶ αὐτῆς ἐρῶ τῆς ἱστορίας ὅτι σεμνότερον αὐτόθεν φαίνεται τὸ τὸν ἐλάττονα καὶ ὑπηρέτην ἀποκεκυλικέναι „τὸν λίθον“ ἢ τὸν ἐπὶ ὠφελείᾳ ἀνθρώπων ἀνιστάμενον τοῦτο πεποιηκέναι. οὐ λέγω δ᾿ ὅτι οἱ μὲν τῷ λόγῳ ἐπιβουλεύοντες καὶ ἀποκτεῖναι αὐτὸν βουληθέντες καὶ δεῖξαι πᾶσι νεκρὸν καὶ τὸ μηδὲν τυγχάνοντα βούλονται αὐτοῦ μηδαμῶς ἀνοιχθῆναι τὸν τάφον, ἵνα μηδεὶς τὸν λόγον μετὰ τὴν ἐπιβουλὴν αὐτῶν ζῶντα θεάσηται· ὁ δὲ ὑπὲρ σωτηρίας ἀνθρώπων ἐπιδημῶν συνεργὸς τοῦ ἀγγέλου ἄγγελος θεοῦ ἰσχυρότερος ὢν τῶν ἐπιβουλευόντων ἀποκυλίει τὸν βαρὺν λίθον· ἵνα πεισθῶσιν οἱ νομίζοντες τεθνηκέναι τὸν λόγον ὅτι „οὐκ ἔστι“ „μετὰ τῶν νεκρῶν“ ἀλλὰ ζῇ καὶ „προάγει“ τοὺς βουλομένους αὐτῷ ἀκολουθεῖν, ἵνα ἐπιδείξηται τὰ ἑξῆς οἷς ἐπεδείξατο πρότερον, τοῖς μὴ χωροῦσί πω αὐτῶν μείζονα κατὰ τὸν πρότερον τῆς εἰσαγωγῆς αὐτῶν χρόνον. εἶτ᾿ οὐκ οἶδ᾿ ὅπως μετὰ ταῦτα παραῤῥίπτει, οὐκ οἶδα εἰς τί τῇ προθέσει αὐτοῦ χρήσιμον εἶναι δοκοῦν, τὸ περὶ τῆς Μαρίας κυούσης ἐληλυθέναι πρὸς τὸν Ἰωσὴφ ἄγγελον καὶ πάλιν ὑπὲρ τοῦ τὸ βρέφος γεννηθὲν καὶ ἐπιβου λευόμενον ἐξαρπάσαντας φυγεῖν εἰς Αἴγυπτον. περὶ τούτων δὲ καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἀνωτέρω πρὸς τὰ ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ εἰρημένα διελέχθημεν. τί δὲ βούλεται Κέλσῳ (τὸ) καὶ Μωϋσεῖ καὶ τοῖς ἄλλοις ἱστορεῖσθαι κατὰ τὰς γραφὰς ἀγγέλους πέμπεσθαι; οὐδὲν γάρ μοι φαίνεται συμβάλλεσθαι αὐτῷ πρὸς ὃ βούλεται, καὶ μάλιστα ἐπεὶ οὐδεὶς μὲν ἐκείνων περὶ τοῦ γένους τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἠγωνίσατο, ἵν᾿ αὐτὸ ἐπιστρέψῃ ὅση δύναμις ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων. καὶ ἄλλοι οὖν πεπέμφθωσαν ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ οὗτός τι πλέον ἀπαγγελλέτω, καὶ πλημμελούντων Ἰουδαίων καὶ μεταχαραττόντων τὴν εὐσέβειαν καὶ οὐχ ὅσια δρώντων τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ μεταδεδωκέτω „ἄλλοις γεωργοῖς,“ τοῖς πανταχοῦ ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις ἑαυτῶν ἐπιμελουμένοις καὶ πάντα πράττουσιν ὑπὲρ τοῦ τὰς ἀπὸ τῆς διδασκαλίας τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἀφορμὰς προσαγαγεῖν διὰ βίου καθαροῦ καὶ λόγου ἀκολούθου τῷ βίῳ πρὸς τὸν τῶν ὅλων θεόν.
thought_title: The angel who rolled away the stone
pass_a_gloss: Celsus accuses (κατηγορεῖ) also the account (λόγος) saying an angel (ἄγγελος) has rolled away (ἀποκεκυλικέναι) from the tomb (τάφος), where Jesus's body (σῶμα) was, 'the stone' (λίθος) [Mt 28:2], like a lad (μειράκιον) who in a school exercise (ἐν διατριβῇ) has received [a task] to accuse someone by the commonplaces (τοπικῶς); and as having found something wise against the account he says: [Celsus:] the child (παῖς) of God, as it seems, was not able to open (ἀνοῖξαι) the tomb but needed (ἐδεήθη) another to move away (ἀποκινήσοντος) the rock (πέτρα). [Origen:] And so that I may not over-busy myself (περιεργάσωμαι) about the details of the place, nor, setting out a tropology (τροπολογία, figurative reading) at present, seem to philosophize (φιλοσοφεῖν) on these out of season (ἀκαίρως), I will speak about the history (ἱστορία) itself: that it appears at once more dignified (σεμνότερον) that the lesser (ἐλάττων) and servant (ὑπηρέτης) rolled away 'the stone' than that the one rising (ἀνιστάμενος) for benefit (ὠφέλεια) of humans did this. I do not say (οὐ λέγω, praeteritio) that those plotting against (ἐπιβουλεύοντες) the Word and wishing to kill him and show to all [him] dead and being nothing wish his tomb by no means to be opened, so that no one may behold the Word alive after their plot (ἐπιβουλή); but the one sojourning (ἐπιδημῶν) for salvation (σωτηρία) of humans, fellow-worker (συνεργός) of the angel, angel of God, being stronger (ἰσχυρότερος) than the plotters, rolls away the heavy (βαρύς) stone, so that those thinking the Word to have died may be persuaded that he 'is not' 'with the dead' [Lk 24:5-6] but lives and 'goes before' (προάγει) [Mt 28:7] those wishing to follow (ἀκολουθεῖν) him, so that he may show the things following (τὰ ἑξῆς) those he showed before, to those not yet containing (χωροῦσι) things greater than these in the earlier time of their introduction (εἰσαγωγή). Then I do not know how after these he throws in (παραῤῥίπτει), I do not know for what seeming useful to his purpose (πρόθεσις), the [story] about Mary being pregnant (κυούσης) that an angel came to Joseph [Mt 1:20], and again for their snatching away (ἐξαρπάσαντας) the babe (βρέφος) born and plotted against to flee into Egypt [Mt 2:13]. About these we argued (διελέχθημεν) also above toward what was said by him. What does it mean (βούλεται) for Celsus that also to Moses and the others angels are recorded (ἱστορεῖσθαι) according to the Scriptures (γραφαί) to be sent (πέμπεσθαι)? For it seems to me to contribute (συμβάλλεσθαι) nothing to him toward what he wants, and especially since none of those contended (ἠγωνίσατο) about the race (γένος) of humans, to turn (ἐπιστρέψῃ) it as far as power allowed from sins (ἁμαρτήματα). Let others then also have been sent (πεπέμφθωσαν, perf. imper.) from God, and let this one announce (ἀπαγγελλέτω) something more (πλέον); and, the Jews offending (πλημμελούντων) and recoining/debasing (μεταχαραττόντων) piety (εὐσέβεια) and doing not holy (ὅσια) things, let him have handed over (μεταδεδωκέτω) the kingdom (βασιλεία) of God to 'other farmers' (γεωργοῖς) [Mt 21:41, 43], those everywhere in the churches (ἐκκλησίαι) caring for themselves and doing all for bringing (προσαγαγεῖν) the starting points (ἀφορμαί) from the teaching (διδασκαλία) of Jesus through a pure (καθαρός) life (βίος) and word (λόγος) consequent (ἀκόλουθος) to the life toward the God of all (τῶν ὅλων).

pass_b_english: Celsus also finds fault with the account which says that an angel rolled away “the stone” (Matthew 28:2) from the tomb where the body of Jesus lay. He goes about it like a schoolboy who has been set, as a classroom exercise, to accuse someone from the stock headings of rhetoric. And as though he had hit upon something clever against the account, he says: “The child of God, it seems, could not open the tomb, but needed someone else to move the rock away.”

I do not want to labour over the details of the passage, nor to seem to philosophize out of season by setting out a figurative interpretation at this point. So I will speak of the narrative itself. On its face it appears more dignified that the lesser one, the servant, should have rolled away “the stone” than that he who was rising for the benefit of human beings should have done it himself. Not to mention that those who plotted against the Word, who wanted to kill him and to show everyone that he was dead and nothing at all, wanted his tomb never to be opened, so that no one might see the Word alive after their plot. But the angel of God, who comes for the salvation of human beings as fellow worker of the Angel, is stronger than the plotters and rolls away the heavy stone. He does this so that those who think the Word is dead may be persuaded that he “is not among the dead” (Luke 24:5–6) but lives and “goes before” (Matthew 28:7) those who wish to follow him. And he goes before them in order to show them what follows on from what he showed them earlier, when, in the first stage of their instruction, they could not yet take in things greater than those.

Then, after this, he somehow throws in, though I do not know what use he thinks it serves his purpose, the story that an angel came to Joseph about Mary when she was with child (Matthew 1:20), and again an angel came so that they would snatch away the newborn child, who was being plotted against, and flee into Egypt (Matthew 2:13). We have already discussed these matters above, in answer to what he said.

And what is Celsus driving at with the fact that the Scriptures record angels being sent to Moses and to the others? It seems to me to contribute nothing to what he wants, especially since none of those angels contended on behalf of the human race to turn it, as far as was possible, from its sins. Grant, then, that others too were sent from God. Let this one proclaim something more. And since the Jews were going astray, debasing true religion, and doing what is unholy, let him hand over the kingdom of God to “other farmers” (Matthew 21:41, 43): to those who everywhere in the churches keep watch over themselves and do everything they can, by a pure life and by words that agree with that life, to bring to the God of all the starting points they have drawn from the teaching of Jesus.
notes: Celsus's mocking sentence is printed as a quotation; the rest is Origen. 'τοπικῶς' = arguing from rhetorical topoi (stock headings), rendered as a schoolroom exercise. 'οὐ λέγω δ᾿ ὅτι' is a praeteritio (he says the thing while saying he does not), rendered 'Not to mention that'. The phrase 'ὁ δὲ ὑπὲρ σωτηρίας ἀνθρώπων ἐπιδημῶν συνεργὸς τοῦ ἀγγέλου ἄγγελος θεοῦ' is difficult: the subject is the angel of God at the tomb; 'fellow worker of the angel' most likely refers to Christ under the title 'Angel' (compare the LXX 'Angel of great counsel', Isaiah 9:5 LXX = Isaiah 9:6 English), so 'Angel' is capitalized; the text may also be faulty here (one might expect τοῦ λόγου). No inline citation is given for that uncertain allusion. 'οὐκ ἔστι μετὰ τῶν νεκρῶν' blends Luke 24:5 ('Why do you seek the living among the dead?') with 24:6 ('he is not here'); 'προάγει' is the angel's message in Matthew 28:7 (also Mark 16:7). 'τοῖς μὴ χωροῦσί πω αὐτῶν μείζονα' taken as 'things greater than these (αὐτῶν), which they could not yet take in'. 'Μωϋσεῖ καὶ τοῖς ἄλλοις' is read as dative of recipients (angels sent to Moses and the others); it could also be dative of agent ('recorded by Moses and the others'). 'ἐκείνων' (none of those) is taken as those earlier messengers. The imperatives πεπέμφθωσαν / ἀπαγγελλέτω / μεταδεδωκέτω are concessive-hortatory ('Grant... let him'). 'ἄλλοις γεωργοῖς' quotes Matthew 21:41; the handing over of the kingdom echoes 21:43. The final clause (bringing the ἀφορμαί from Jesus's teaching to God) is rendered literally; the object of προσαγαγεῖν is the starting points themselves.

Open doubt (review): 5.58 crux 'ὁ δὲ ὑπὲρ σωτηρίας ἀνθρώπων ἐπιδημῶν συνεργὸς τοῦ ἀγγέλου ἄγγελος θεοῦ': I kept the printed grammar and the capital 'Angel' for Christ, because in 5.52-58 Celsus speaks of Jesus as an angel sent from God. The text may be corrupt (one might expect τοῦ λόγου); translator_notes records this. Verdict is pass.
